title: Authoritative rows and lists
summary: Lists, tables and worklists are first-class semantic collections. Render 0/1/N rows from an explicit collection contract; keep count separate; use stable server-owned row identity; never derive transaction authority from row position or displayed values.
invariants: A collection slot and a numeric count are different facts. Never overload one value to mean both.
Row identity is a stable server-owned semantic identity, never visible position, DOM index or current sort position.
0, 1 and N rows are equally ordinary states and must be covered by regression tests.
Missing or duplicate semantic identities fail closed for actionable collections.
If an explicit count is projected, count/collection disagreement is an invalid state rather than an empty list.
Displayed row fields are presentation evidence and do not become command parameters merely because the browser can see them.
Application code should consume the shared Wire collection implementation rather than inventing a private list renderer.

provenance.claim: Compiled authoritative row-collection contract and Federation-company baseline.
Renderer consumes explicit row contract, stable identity, count validation, selection and action boundaries.
